# PATINA

> PATINA marks one Bitcoin output as the carrier of an artifact. Depth is
> the number of blocks that output has stayed unspent. Move it and depth
> returns to zero, and the finished stretch is engraved as a ring that
> cannot be rewritten.

There is no PATINA marketplace. The Bitcoin Universe capability snapshot
records no marketplace surface for PATINA, so no Bitcoin Universe product
implements a buy, sell or settle path for an artifact. Minting happens in
the Bitcoin Universe app; everything else is your own wallet and your own
node.

Every link below is published by this site.

## Public pages

- [PATINA, a Bitcoin artifact that deepens while it sits still](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/index.html): PATINA marks one Bitcoin output as the carrier of an artifact. Depth is the number of blocks that output has stayed unspent. Move it and depth returns to zero, and the finished stretch is engraved as a ring that cannot be rewritten.
- [How depth works, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/depth.html): Depth is the number of blocks a PATINA carrier output has stayed unspent. Take an artifact apart part by part, watch a stretch close into a ring, and see why an artifact at depth forty can still carry four years of history.
- [The tier journey, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/tiers.html): Eight tiers from Raw to Elder, each one a band of depth with an exact block threshold. Raw at 0, Sheen at 1008, Cast at 4032, Verdigris at 12960, Umber at 26280, Bronze at 52560, Oxide at 105120 and Elder at 210000 blocks.
- [Firstlight Seals, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/firstlight.html): Firstlight Seals are the founding PATINA artifacts. They can only be created inside one commit window of 4032 blocks. No team allocation, no price to the project, and at least 100 000 sats of your own bitcoin sealed in as the endowment.
- [Commit, wait, reveal, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/mint.html): How a Firstlight Seal is claimed: publish a commit output, let it age at least 144 blocks, then reveal. No price, network fees only, and at least 100 000 sats of your own bitcoin sealed inside as the endowment.
- [Protocol, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/protocol.html): The PATINA mechanism for a developer: marker bytes, the commit leaf, the commit and reveal shapes, the SEED check order, successor selection and the default rule, rings, identifier derivations, reorg behaviour and the frozen reason code registry.
- [Verify it yourself, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/verify.html): Read a PATINA artifact's depth off your own Bitcoin node, decode a marker by hand, recompute an artifact id, query an indexer, run the index yourself, and set two indexers against each other. Real commands, no trust in us.
- [Transparency, who holds authority over PATINA and what it reaches](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/transparency.html): Supply with no plan behind it, zero allocations, the authority table, what is frozen and what can change, what the kill switches can and cannot reach, and live concentration figures read from a connected indexer.
- [Risks, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/risks.html): Every way PATINA can disappoint you, in one place: depth is not provenance, founding membership can be concentrated, buying resets depth, a wallet can spend a carrier by accident, and nobody owes this anything.
- [Questions people actually ask, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/faq.html): Plain answers about PATINA: what depth is, why moving resets it, what a Firstlight Seal costs, what happens when a carrier is spent below the minimum, whether a bundle can be split, and what an attestation does not prove.
- [Press and brand, PATINA](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/press.html): Brand assets for PATINA: wordmark, protocol mark, favicon and social cards as SVG, a short description, a longer description, the palette in hex, and the rules for using any of it.

The documentation is at https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/ and is organised into the sections
below. Each page states its kind: introductory explains, operational is a
procedure, normative is the rule as the specification states it, and
generated means every printed value is computed and checked against the
golden vectors.

## Start here

I want to understand PATINA. What an artifact is, what you own, and where the edges are.

- [What PATINA is](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/index.html): The one sentence, then the long version. Marked introductory.
- [Firstlight Seals](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/start/firstlight-seals.html): The founding cohort and how minting works. Marked introductory.
- [What you actually own](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/start/what-you-own.html): An outpoint, an endowment, and a history. Marked introductory.
- [What it does not promise](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/start/limits.html): The honest boundaries, stated up front. Marked introductory.

## Using it

I want a Seal, or I already own an artifact. Wallet setup, the mint, reading your artifact, and what to do when it goes wrong.

- [Wallet setup](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/wallet-setup.html): What your wallet must be able to do. Marked operational.
- [Mint walkthrough](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/mint.html): Commit, wait 144 blocks, reveal. Marked operational.
- [Reading your artifact](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/artifact-page.html): Every field on the artifact page. Marked operational.
- [What resets depth](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/depth-resets.html): The full list, and the one case that does not. Marked operational.
- [Attestations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/attestations.html): Prove the key is still alive. Marked operational.
- [Transferring an artifact](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/transfer.html): Any move resets depth to zero. Marked operational.
- [When something goes wrong](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/using/recovery.html): Stuck reveals, wrong vouts, lost salts. Marked operational.

## Protocol reference

I want to verify an artifact, byte by byte. The grammar, the checks in order, the state machine, and every reason code.

- [Identity and derivations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/identity.html): Domain tags and worked byte examples. Marked generated.
- [Marker grammar](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/marker-grammar.html): The byte table and the selection rule. Marked generated.
- [SEED rules](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/seed-rules.html): Six checks, in order. Marked normative.
- [KEEP and the default rule](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/keep-rules.html): How a successor is chosen. Marked normative.
- [State machine](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/state-machine.html): ALIVE, RELIC, and the transitions between. Marked normative.
- [Rings](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/rings.html): How a completed stretch is engraved. Marked normative.
- [Depth and tiers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/depth-and-tiers.html): The full table with elapsed time. Marked normative.
- [Reason codes](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/reason-codes.html): All eighteen, and what each means for you. Marked normative.
- [Reorg behavior](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/reorgs.html): Rollback, replay, and finality. Marked normative.
- [The upgrade boundary](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/protocol/upgrade-boundary.html): What can change and what cannot. Marked normative.

- [Run your own indexer](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/docs/api/run-an-indexer.html): From a Bitcoin node to a served API. Marked operational.

## Specification and vectors

- [patina-protocol.md](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/patina-protocol.md): the specification the
  deployment records and the golden vectors bind to by SHA-256.
- [vectors/golden.json](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/vectors/golden.json): the golden vectors two
  implementations compare against.
- [vectors/manifest.json](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/patina/vectors/manifest.json): what the vector set
  covers, and the specification hash it was produced from.
